author: Arthur Security <security@arthur.ai>
_comment: Scope: HIGH/CRITICAL findings that a container-image re-scan still reports for the genai-engine, ml-engine and genai-engine-models-* images AND that are not exploitable in our usage. Every statement here is 'not_affected' with a justification. Remediated CVEs are excluded by policy — fix, don't justify (security/README.md), so a CVE disappearing from this document means it was fixed, not dropped. Remediated and therefore absent: python3.11 is removed from every image (its dpkg metadata deleted); litellm/langsmith/msgpack/nltk/uv/pyasn1 are upgraded past their advisories; libexpat1 is at 2.5.0-1+deb12u4 in every image as of 2026-10-02, which fixes CVE-2026-45186, CVE-2025-59375, CVE-2026-25210 and CVE-2026-66046, so their statements were removed; models-gcs is rebuilt with perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u4 and libpcre2-8-0 10.42-1+deb12u2 as of 2026-10-05, which fix CVE-2026-42496, CVE-2026-42497, CVE-2026-48962, CVE-2026-8376, CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-57433, CVE-2026-57432 and CVE-2026-103111, so their statements were removed (perl CVE-2026-9538 is still unfixed in bookworm and keeps its statement); and as of 2026-07-30 the distroless OS-package findings (libc6, libssl3, libkrb5*, liblzma5) are fixed at the source — the build stages now mirror the base's /lib layout with their apt-upgraded libraries and rewrite /var/lib/dpkg/status.d to the versions actually installed, so the patched objects ship and scanners read true versions. Auditor note: the distroless base is not merged-/usr, so before that change `COPY /usr/lib` never reached the glibc and liblzma objects the base keeps in /lib. Images up to and including 2.1.754 shipped the base's unpatched glibc (2.36-9+deb12u13) and liblzma5 (5.4.1-1), and earlier revisions of this document incorrectly recorded those libc6 CVEs as fixed. The libssl3 and krb5 objects do live under /usr/lib and were genuinely patched throughout; only their dpkg metadata was stale. See genai-engine/dockerfile, ml-engine/Dockerfile, deployment/model-upload/Dockerfile and PR #2073. Audited 2026-08-18 against the per-image Trivy reports from the daily image-vuln-scan: (a) no remaining statement suppresses a finding that has an upstream fix — every one is unfixed at the installed version, so none is masking a bump we could take instead; (b) the python3.11 statements (CVE-2025-69534, CVE-2026-3644, CVE-2026-4224, CVE-2026-6100, CVE-2026-7210, CVE-2025-13836) were removed because the runtime-s3 and runtime-fs stages now delete the interpreter and its dpkg metadata outright, so the packages are absent and those statements matched nothing; (c) the document is scoped to HIGH/CRITICAL, so four statements were removed for falling below that line: CVE-2026-11822 and CVE-2026-11824 (libsqlite3-0) and CVE-2026-56131 and CVE-2026-56407 (libexpat1) were re-rated from HIGH to MEDIUM in the vulnerability database. Note what this does and does not mean: those four are NOT remediated. The packages are still installed at the same versions and Debian still ships no fix (it marks the sqlite pair <postponed> for bookworm); they simply sit under the scan's --severity HIGH,CRITICAL filter, so nothing reports them today. If any of them is ever re-rated back to HIGH it will surface as an untriaged finding and will need its justification restored -- the reasoning was sound, only the severity changed. Updated 2026-10-28 against the daily Trivy reports for 2.1.1073-dev and an external scan of 2.1.980: CVE-2026-84782 (libssl3) was removed because bookworm-security now ships the fix in 3.0.22-1~deb12u2. genai-engine-cpu/gpu and ml-engine already carry it; the models images had been re-tagged rather than rebuilt and are rebuilt by this change. CVE-2026-81726 (nltk) was removed because nltk 3.10.4, now shipped, is the patched release: the maintainer advisory (nltk/nltk GHSA-8mgp-746c-j5xp) lists <=3.10.3 as affected and 3.10.4 as patched, and the fix commits it references (2a92b71, a44a7af, cbc9845; PRs #3757, #3759, #3813) are all contained in the v3.10.4 tag. Fixed rather than justified: aiohttp, Authlib, brotli, certifi, oauthlib, pillow, virtualenv and uv (0.13.6, GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62), plus filelock in the models images. Added: CVE-2026-112940 (filelock, capped below 4.0 by litellm), CVE-2026-72848 (langchain-community, no fix), CVE-2026-115506 (libexpat1, no fix) and CVE-2026-85091 (zlib1g, version not affected). Updated 2026-10-30: added CVE-2026-111497 (brotli bundled in the pillow wheel, no fixed Pillow release). Updated 2026-11-13 against the daily Trivy reports for 2.1.1107-dev and an external scan of genai-engine-gpu 2.1.1078. Removed as fixed: CVE-2026-112940 (filelock) -- litellm 1.108.3 widened its cap to filelock<5 and snowflake-connector-python 4.8.1 dropped its <4 cap, so genai-engine and ml-engine now ship filelock 4.2.10. Removed because Debian re-triaged them as not affecting bookworm, so no scanner reports them any more: CVE-2026-76642, CVE-2026-78408 and CVE-2026-78409 (util-linux) and CVE-2026-14456 (openssl). Fixed rather than justified: pyasn1 0.6.5 (CVE-2026-119194..119197) and truststore 0.10.5 (GHSA-pmqj-r2x2-vx88); pypdf was already at 6.21.4. CVE-2026-85091 (zlib1g) was re-justified from vulnerable_code_not_present to vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path: its 1.3.1.2+ version range is disputed upstream and Debian lists bookworm as vulnerable. Added, all unfixed in bookworm: 14 krb5 CVEs (CVE-2026-107364, CVE-2026-112315..112323, CVE-2026-118380, CVE-2026-119079, CVE-2026-71199, CVE-2026-71200), libexpat1 CVE-2026-113351, CVE-2026-117610 and CVE-2026-118370, libsqlite3-0 CVE-2026-119373, CVE-2026-119374 and CVE-2026-119379, zlib1g CVE-2026-76844, and libc6 CVE-2026-84243.

statements._comment: zlib1g: The overflow is in MiniZip (zlib contrib/minizip), which upstream states is not a supported part of zlib. Debian's zlib1g shared library does not build or export the MiniZip code (the vulnerable zipOpenNewFileInZip4_64 symbol is absent); Arthur links only the core inflate/deflate API. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: The overflow is in MiniZip (zlib contrib/minizip), which upstream states is not a supported part of zlib. Debian's zlib1g shared library does not build or export the MiniZip code (the vulnerable zipOpenNewFileInZip4_64 symbol is absent); Arthur links only the core inflate/deflate API.

statements._comment: ncurses: The buffer overflow is in the infocmp CLI / terminfo handling. The images run a non-interactive service with no TTY; Arthur never invokes infocmp nor renders attacker-controlled terminal/terminfo data. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: The buffer overflow is in the infocmp CLI / terminfo handling. The images run a non-interactive service with no TTY; Arthur never invokes infocmp nor renders attacker-controlled terminal/terminfo data.

statements._comment: libsqlite3-0: Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL. Exploitation requires executing crafted SQL (KeyInfoFromExprList), which is not in the engine's data path. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL. Exploitation requires executing crafted SQL (KeyInfoFromExprList), which is not in the engine's data path.

statements._comment: perl-base: perl-base is a transitive base-OS package on the models-gcs image; no Arthur process invokes the Perl interpreter or Archive::Tar. The upload job runs a single Python entrypoint (upload_models.py). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: perl-base is a transitive base-OS package on the models-gcs image; no Arthur process invokes the Perl interpreter or Archive::Tar. The upload job runs a single Python entrypoint (upload_models.py).

statements._comment: util-linux (libblkid1 and sibling packages): CVE-2026-53615 is an integer overflow in libblkid's DOS/MBR partition parser (partitions/dos.c, parse_dos_extended); no Debian bookworm fix is available (bookworm ships 2.38.1-5+deb12u3, still vulnerable; Debian bug #1140197). Triggering requires libblkid to probe an attacker-controlled block device / disk image / partition table. These images never probe disks or mount untrusted media — the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes to cloud storage / a mounted volume. Subcomponents are name-only so the statement matches whichever util-linux binary packages a given image ships (distroless images carry only libuuid1; the slim models-gcs runtime carries the full set). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-53615 is an integer overflow in libblkid's DOS/MBR partition-table parser (partitions/dos.c). It is reachable only when libblkid probes an attacker-controlled block device, disk image, or partition table. These images never probe disks or mount untrusted media: the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage / a mounted volume. No Debian bookworm fix is available yet.

statements._comment: libacl1: CVE-2026-54369 is a symlink-traversal privilege escalation in libacl's pathname-based functions (acl_get_file/acl_set_file/acl_extended_file/acl_delete_def_file follow symlinks); no Debian bookworm fix is available (bookworm ships acl 2.3.1-3, no-dsa/postponed; fixed upstream in acl 2.4.0). Exploitation requires a local unprivileged attacker racing a higher-privileged process that operates on ACLs of attacker-controllable paths. The models-gcs image runs a single non-interactive Python entrypoint (upload_models.py) as one user with no other local users and performs no ACL operations on untrusted paths. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-54369 is a local symlink-traversal privilege escalation in libacl's pathname-based functions. It requires a local unprivileged attacker and a higher-privileged process performing ACL operations on attacker-controllable paths. The models-gcs image runs a single non-interactive Python entrypoint (upload_models.py) as one user, has no other local users, and performs no ACL operations on untrusted paths. No Debian bookworm fix is available yet (fixed upstream in acl 2.4.0).

statements._comment: gzip: CVE-2026-41992 is a global buffer overflow (OOB read) from improperly reused global state between the LZW and LZH decoders in a single gzip invocation; no Debian bookworm fix is available (bookworm ships gzip 1.12-1, no-dsa/postponed). Triggering requires feeding gzip a crafted LZW file followed by a crafted LZH file in one command. The models-gcs image never invokes gzip on attacker-controlled .lzw/.lzh archives — the upload job downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage. gzip is a transitive base-OS package. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-41992 is an out-of-bounds read from reused global state between gzip's LZW and LZH decoders, triggered only by decompressing a crafted LZW file followed by a crafted LZH file in a single gzip invocation. The models-gcs image never invokes gzip on attacker-controlled archives; gzip is a transitive base-OS package and the upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage. No Debian bookworm fix is available yet.

statements._comment: libsqlite3-0: CVE-2026-11822 is arbitrary code execution via crafted FTS5 full-text search data. Justification restored — this statement was removed on 2026-08-18 only because the CVE had been re-rated HIGH to MEDIUM and fell below this document's severity scope; it has since been re-rated back to HIGH and resurfaced as an untriaged finding, exactly as that audit note anticipated. The reasoning is unchanged: persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector), libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and the engines never use FTS5. Debian marks the sqlite3 pair postponed for bookworm, so no fix is available at 3.40.1-2+deb12u2. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-02.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-11822 requires supplying crafted FTS5 full-text search data to SQLite. Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and no FTS5 functionality is used. No Debian bookworm fix is available (postponed).

statements._comment: libsqlite3-0: CVE-2026-11824 is a heap-based buffer overflow in FTS5 enabling arbitrary code execution or a crash. Justification restored — removed on 2026-08-18 only for falling below the HIGH/CRITICAL scope after a HIGH to MEDIUM re-rating, and now re-rated back to HIGH. The reasoning is unchanged: persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector), libsqlite3 is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and FTS5 is not used. Debian marks the sqlite3 pair postponed for bookworm, so no fix is available at 3.40.1-2+deb12u2. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-02.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-11824 is a heap-based buffer overflow reachable only through SQLite's FTS5 module. Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and FTS5 is not used. No Debian bookworm fix is available (postponed).

statements._comment: util-linux (libuuid1 and sibling packages): CVE-2026-53613 is a TOCTOU race in the mount program via an ancestor-directory swap on the target path. Bookworm ships 2.38.1-5+deb12u3 and the security tracker still lists util-linux as open, so no fix is available. This is a sibling of the already-justified CVE-2026-53615 in the same package set at the same version. Exploitation requires invoking mount(8) against a path an adversary can restructure concurrently; these images never call mount at runtime — the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes to cloud storage or an already-mounted volume. Subcomponents are name-only so the statement matches whichever util-linux binary packages a given image ships (distroless images carry only libuuid1; the slim models-gcs runtime carries the full set). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-02.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-53613 is a TOCTOU race in mount(8) requiring an adversary to swap an ancestor directory of the mount target during the call. These images never invoke mount at runtime: the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage / an already-mounted volume. No Debian bookworm fix is available.

statements._comment: util-linux: CVE-2026-78410, one of four util-linux advisories reported against 2.38.1-5+deb12u3 (with CVE-2026-76642, CVE-2026-78408, CVE-2026-78409). Debian lists util-linux as open for it, so no fix exists. Reachability is the same as the other util-linux statements: mount/umount and libblkid device probing are never exercised by these images. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-09.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-78410 is reachable only through util-linux code paths these images never execute: the mount/umount programs and libblkid's probing of block devices, disk images and partition tables. The engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage / an already-mounted volume. Bookworm ships no fix at the installed 2.38.1-5+deb12u3.

statements._comment: libsystemd0 / libudev1: CVE-2026-16742 is reported against systemd 252.39-1~deb12u2 on the models-gcs image, the only image carrying these packages; the Debian security tracker lists systemd as open, so no fix is available. No Arthur process runs systemd, systemd-udevd or any systemd daemon — the images have no init system and the model-upload job runs a single Python entrypoint (upload_models.py). libsystemd0 and libudev1 are present only as transitive shared-library dependencies of other base packages, and their client APIs are never called. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-09.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-16742 affects systemd, which these images never run: there is no init system and the model-upload job runs a single Python entrypoint. libsystemd0 and libudev1 ship only as transitive shared-library dependencies of other base packages and their APIs are never called. Debian ships no fix at the installed 252.39-1~deb12u2.

statements._comment: langchain-community: CVE-2026-72848 is an SSRF in SitemapLoader.parse_sitemap, which applies restrict_to_same_domain to leaf <url> entries but not to nested <sitemap> entries, so an attacker-controlled sitemap can make the server fetch an internal URL. Reported against 0.4.2 (genai-engine/pyproject.toml). The advisory marks every release as affected with no patched version, so there is no upgrade to take. genai-engine never constructs SitemapLoader, WebBaseLoader or any langchain_community document loader (grep of genai-engine/src for SitemapLoader/sitemap finds nothing outside tokenizer vocabularies), so no sitemap is ever fetched or parsed. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-04-28, or as soon as a fixed langchain-community is released.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-72848 is reachable only through langchain-community's SitemapLoader. The engine never instantiates SitemapLoader or any other langchain_community web document loader, so no sitemap is fetched and the missing domain check is never exercised. No patched release exists.

statements._comment: libexpat1: CVE-2026-115506 is a CPU-exhaustion DoS — expat's billion-laughs accounting (accountingDiffTolerated) trips too late, so a moderately sized XML document with a large DTD and nested entities costs tens of seconds of CPU per parse. Reported against 2.5.0-1+deb12u4 by an external scanner; the images now ship 2.5.0-1+deb12u5, and the advisory covers every libexpat through 2.9.0 with no fix, so there is no upgrade to take. No Arthur code parses XML (no xml.*, lxml, defusedxml, ElementTree or pyexpat use in genai-engine/src or ml-engine/src), and no API accepts XML input. The only XML parsed at runtime is cloud SDK response bodies (botocore for S3, Azure SDK) received over TLS from the provider's endpoint, which an attacker cannot author. Impact is bounded CPU on a single request, with no memory corruption or data exposure. models-gcs does not ship libexpat1. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-04-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-115506 requires the attacker to supply an XML document with a crafted DTD. No Arthur code or API parses XML; expat is reached only when cloud SDKs parse response bodies received over TLS from the provider's own endpoint, which an attacker cannot control. Impact would be bounded CPU per parse. No fixed libexpat release exists.

statements._comment: zlib1g: CVE-2026-85091 is a heap overflow in gz_vacate() when gzprintf()/gzvprintf() follow a stalled non-blocking gzwrite(). The NVD text scopes it to zlib 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2, where non-blocking support was added (upstream commit 81cc0be), and this statement previously claimed the code was absent from bookworm's 1.2.13 on that basis. That claim is withdrawn: upstream discussion (madler/zlib#1310) notes the PoC is triggerable before that commit too, Debian lists bookworm 1:1.2.13.dfsg-1 as vulnerable, and the fix (df84af2, zlib 1.4) is the same change that fixes CVE-2026-76844. The justification is now that the code is not reached. Exploitation needs a process that writes a gzip file through zlib's gz* file API (gzwrite/gzprintf/gzputs) and keeps writing after an underlying write() failure. The engines' Python processes never use that API: Python's gzip and zlib modules implement gzip framing in Python over zlib's deflate/inflate stream API, and ml-engine's only gzip use (discovery/endpoint/envelope.py, discovery/_vendor/classify.py) goes through those modules. A dynamic-symbol scan (nm -D --undefined-only) of the ml-engine and genai-engine-cpu image filesystems finds gzwrite imported only by CLI tools the services never invoke: pg_dump, pg_basebackup and the other postgresql-client tools, wget, libapt-pkg and binutils' libctf; pyarrow's libarrow does not import it. Debian ships no bookworm fix (trixie is fixed by DSA-6613-1). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-05-13.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-85091 is reachable only through zlib's gz* file-write API (gzwrite followed by gzprintf). The engine services never call it: Python's gzip and zlib modules use the deflate/inflate stream API, and the only binaries importing gzwrite are CLI tools (postgresql-client, wget, apt, binutils) that the services never run. No bookworm fix exists.

statements._comment: pillow: CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder, fixed upstream in brotli 1.0.10 / 1.1.1 / 1.2.1. genai-engine ships Pillow only as a transitive dependency (bert-score -> matplotlib -> pillow), and every Pillow wheel through the latest release, 13.0.0, bundles the vulnerable brotli 1.2.0 in pillow.libs (libbrotlidec/libbrotlicommon .so.1.2.0). In both the 12.3.0 and 13.0.0 manylinux x86_64 wheels the only object that links libbrotlidec is the bundled libfreetype, and the only Pillow module that links libfreetype is PIL._imagingft (ImageFont); FreeType uses Brotli solely to decompress WOFF2 fonts. genai-engine code never imports PIL or matplotlib, and the installed packages that call ImageFont (transformers' pix2struct and ernie4_5_vl_moe processors, pygments' image formatter, torch's tensorboard summary) are not used by the engine, which loads only text models. No path loads a font, let alone an attacker-supplied WOFF2 one. ml-engine and the models images do not ship Pillow. The python brotli package in genai-engine/uv.lock is in the performance dependency group and is not installed in the images. Tracked in UP-5303. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-30, or as soon as a Pillow release bundles brotli >= 1.2.1.
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable Brotli decoder bundled in Pillow's wheel is reachable only through FreeType's WOFF2 font decompression, which Pillow exposes via ImageFont. genai-engine never renders text with Pillow or matplotlib and never loads a font, so the decoder is never called. Pillow is present only as a transitive dependency of bert-score's plotting helpers. No Pillow release with a fixed brotli exists yet (13.0.0 still bundles 1.2.0).

statements._comment: krb5: CVE-2026-107364 is an unauthenticated KDC read overrun in the krb5 ASN.1 decoder. Every image ships only the MIT krb5 client libraries (libkrb5-3, libgssapi-krb5-2, libk5crypto3, libkrb5support0), present only as transitive shared-library dependencies of other packages. No image installs krb5-kdc, krb5-admin-server, krb5-pkinit, libkadm5srv/libkadm5clnt, libkdb5 or libgssrpc4 (checked against the per-image CycloneDX SBOMs), so no KDC or kadmind runs and the server-side code is absent. Kerberos is also never used as a client: the images carry no krb5.conf, keytab or credential cache, PostgreSQL connections authenticate with password/TLS, and no Arthur code references Kerberos or GSSAPI (grep of genai-engine/src and ml-engine/src for kerberos/gssapi/gssencmode/krb5/Trusted_Connection finds nothing). Debian lists every krb5 release, bookworm included, as vulnerable with no fix (bug 1153598). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-05-13.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-107364 is an unauthenticated KDC read overrun in the krb5 ASN.1 decoder. These images run no KDC, and the client libraries never perform a Kerberos exchange (no krb5.conf, keytab or credential cache; no Kerberos or GSSAPI authentication configured), so the vulnerable path is never reached. No bookworm fix exists.

statements._comment: libexpat1: CVE-2026-113351 is a DoS in which XML_ParserReset fails to offset tracked allocations, so a large document makes later documents on the same reset parser fail with XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY (Debian: bookworm <postponed>, minor issue). statements._comment: zlib1g: CVE-2026-76844 is a heap overflow in gz_write(): after an underlying write() fails, strm.next_in is left pointing at the caller's buffer and a later gz* write overruns a heap allocation. It affects zlib 1.2.11 through 1.3.2, so bookworm's 1:1.2.13.dfsg-1 is affected, and Debian ships no bookworm fix (trixie is fixed by DSA-6613-1). Exploitation needs a process that writes a gzip file through zlib's gz* file API (gzwrite/gzprintf/gzputs) and keeps writing after an underlying write() failure. The engines' Python processes never use that API: Python's gzip and zlib modules implement gzip framing in Python over zlib's deflate/inflate stream API, and ml-engine's only gzip use (discovery/endpoint/envelope.py, discovery/_vendor/classify.py) goes through those modules. A dynamic-symbol scan (nm -D --undefined-only) of the ml-engine and genai-engine-cpu image filesystems finds gzwrite imported only by CLI tools the services never invoke: pg_dump, pg_basebackup and the other postgresql-client tools, wget, libapt-pkg and binutils' libctf; pyarrow's libarrow does not import it. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-05-13.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-76844 is reachable only through zlib's gz* file-write API. The engine services never call it: Python's gzip and zlib modules use the deflate/inflate stream API, and the only binaries importing gzwrite are CLI tools (postgresql-client, wget, apt, binutils) that the services never run. No bookworm fix exists.

statements._comment: libc6: CVE-2026-84243: glibc's gettext accepts LANGUAGE entries containing '/' or '..', so an attacker who can set LANGUAGE in a program's environment can make it load a crafted .mo catalog from an arbitrary path. Reported against libc6 2.36-9+deb12u14 (and libc-bin on models-gcs); Debian lists every release as vulnerable with no fix. Trivy rates it MEDIUM; it is recorded here because the external scanner rates it HIGH. The environment of every engine process is set by the deployer (Helm values, docker-compose, CloudFormation) and is not reachable from any API: no Arthur code spawns a subprocess with caller-supplied environment variables (the only os.environ writes set TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM). An attacker who can already set a process's environment variables controls the deployment. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-05-13.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-84243 requires the attacker to set the LANGUAGE environment variable of a process. Engine process environments are fixed by the deployer and are not reachable through any API, and no Arthur code starts a subprocess with caller-supplied environment. No fix exists.
